QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_59

question.text: FCFF of INR 15 crore/year for 5 years plus terminal value of INR 200 crore at 12% WACC gives approximate EV of:

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook explains DCF as valuing a company by discounting forecast free cash flows at WACC and adding the discounted terminal value, with Enterprise Value = PV of forecast FCFFs + PV of terminal value. At 12% WACC, PV of five INR 15 crore FCFFs is approximately 15 x 3.6048 = INR 54.1 crore; PV of INR 200 crore terminal value at the end of year 5 is approximately 200 / (1.12)^5 = 200 x 0.5674 = INR 113.5 crore. Sum is approximately INR 167.6 crore. The Trap: "Less than INR 100 crore" ignores the bulk contributed by the terminal value. "Exactly INR 275 crore" is the undiscounted sum (15 x 5 + 200), forgetting to discount. "More than INR 500 crore" is fabricated. Note: The earlier explanation was generic placeholder text. It has been replaced with the source-backed DCF calculation: PV of five FCFFs plus PV of terminal value approximates INR 167 crore.
